# Curio

> Ryan O'Connor's free guide for people figuring out what AI means for their actual work. Four focuses to move toward, five fallacies that get in the way, a free 90-second quiz, and an on-site chat. Tagline: a guide for the AI uncertain.

Curio is teaching. Nothing is for sale: there is no consulting offer, no paid
product, no funnel and no email gate. The quiz, the starter pack and the chat are free.

## The four focuses

Whatever someone wants from AI tends to be one of four things. Each has its own page.

1. **Inspiration** (`/Inspiration.html`): where this is all going. North-star framing, speculative thinking. "Stop asking what to learn. Ask what to become."
2. **Filter** (`/Filter.html`): what to use and what to ignore. The missing thing is a hierarchy of attention, by timing and by fit.
3. **Mindset** (`/Mindset.html`): for people already using AI who have plateaued. The path runs ask, brief, connect, train, delegate, and context is what moves you along it.
4. **Solutions** (`/Solutions.html`): hand AI the task. Software made for the need, and small tools you describe and get back the same day.

## The five fallacies

Five things people say to themselves about AI. Each feels like a reason, and each
maps to one of the four focuses.

1. **Exhaustion**: "I don't have time." The tool is the time. Answered by Filter.
2. **Guilt**: "Is this cheating?" You set the dial: how much AI does, and how much you keep. Answered by Solutions.
3. **Identity**: "I'm the [Excel] person." The making moves; taste and judgment stay. Answered by Inspiration.
4. **Muscle memory**: "Some day I'll be good at AI." There is no curriculum and no someday. Answered by Mindset.
5. **Yesterday**: "I tried it eight months ago and it got it wrong." That snapshot is old. Answered by Mindset.

## Recurring ideas

- General intelligence comes with the model and improves for everyone at once. What AI knows about you and your work starts at zero and only grows if you build it.
- People who use AI daily report it does half the task, sometimes 80%, and their part is checking, choosing and judgment. That work is tiring in a new way, which is normal.
- On the "AI bubble": whether AI stocks are priced right is a question for investors; whether the tools work is something anyone can test at their desk.

## Pages

- [Home](https://curio.help/): the intro and the hub holding all four focuses, the chat, and all five fallacies.
- [About](https://curio.help/about): why Curio exists and the experience behind it.
- [Quiz](https://curio.help/quiz): free, 90 seconds, no email. Returns your primary fallacy and a direct download of the Curio Starter (a PDF and a Claude skill).
- [Ask Curio](https://curio.help/): the chat, on every page. Free, no signup.

## Who wrote it

Ryan O'Connor. Fifteen years of teaching and directing creative work, with an
architecture background. He brought Claude into a forty-person agency and reached
roughly 75% daily usage within four weeks; the same work raised about $433K in
cost-recovery *questions* (findings, not banked savings) by connecting Claude to
Excel, Asana and the agency's financial system.

- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ryantoconnor/
- Substack: https://curioco.substack.com

## What Curio is not

Curio is not consulting, a course, a cohort, a Discord, or a product for sale.
